The graphs of the functions $y=f(x)$ and $y=h(x)$ are given above. Find ${p}^{′}(0)$ where $p(x)=f(x)h(x).$

${p}^{′}(0)=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The product rule for derivatives gives

$$
{p}^{′}(x)={f}^{′}(x)\cdot h(x)+f(x)\cdot {h}^{′}(x).
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{p}^{′}(0)={f}^{′}(0)\cdot h(0)+f(0)\cdot {h}^{′}(0).
$$

From the graphs above, we obtain that $f(0)=-1$ and $h(0)=-3.$

Additionally,

- The slope of $f(x)$ on $x\in (-2,1)$ equals $-1.$ So, ${f}^{′}(0)=-1.$

- The slope of $h(x)$ on $x\in (-2,1)$ equals $-1.$ So, ${h}^{′}(0)=-1.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}^{′}(0) & ={f}^{′}(0)\cdot h(0)+f(0)\cdot {h}^{′}(0) \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-3)+(-1)\cdot (-1) \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
